title: A bounded elapsed-time contract for the daemon's read path: context-first store getters, a 10s request deadline reaching the blocking call, an explicit 503/Timeout class, a busy_timeout lock policy, sanitized 500 bodies, and a ratchet pinning the 11 residual deadline-free reads

ai-check is CWD-SENSITIVE. Run from repo root with a repo-root-relative module path. The wrong cwd returns LDR001 module-not-found, which reads as a KILL ON EVERY ARM. Always run a pristine known-positive control first.

features.name: Store layer: context-first getters, QueryRowContext, busy_timeout DSN injection, the 86-site migration, and the ratchet
features.description: The five daemon-read-path getters (GetObject:467, GetWorld:522, GetLogEntry:551, GetRegistryHead:628, SelectedHead:802) become context-first and route through s.db.QueryRowContext. writeDSN/readOnlyDSN (writer_lock.go:176/187) inject _pragma=busy_timeout(2000) when the caller's DSN did not set one. The 22 non-test and 64 test call sites migrate. New host/store/context_read_test.go carries TestReadGettersHonorContext (5 subtests), TestProductionDSNSetsBusyTimeout, TestReadRetriesUnderTransientExclusiveLock (with a PRE-REGISTERED outcome record) and TestNoNewDeadlineFreeStoreReads (the section 2.8 ratchet). Daemon BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED after M1 - a request context without a deadline is exactly today's bound - which is what makes M1 independently landable.
features.notes: M1 COMPLETE, T1.1-T1.9 all landed. Final-tree gates: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.6 go build ./... rc=0; go test ./... -count=1 rc=0 (17 packages ok, 0 FAIL); go vet ./... rc=0; gofmt clean. Classify by the CONTEXT, not by error text: check ctx.Err() != nil FIRST, then fall through to Internal. The driver's interrupt path can surface as SQLITE_INTERRUPT which does NOT wrap context.DeadlineExceeded, so errors.Is-only classification misfiles real timeouts as 500s. errors.Is is checked as well, but the context is the authority.

blockingStore must override ALL FIVE getters (reviewer A2's verbatim fix). A one-getter fake lets the other five routes fall through to the embedded real store, answer 200 instantly, and SPURIOUSLY RED the 503 assertion.

Watchdog rule B2: layer 3's red path is t.Error THEN close(escape). Under MU2 the fake's context is Background-derived and would otherwise stay parked until the 10s deadline. The escape return must be a DISTINCT SENTINEL that can never be read as a pass.
TestReadCtxCancelledAfterHandler must leave readDeadline at its 10s DEFAULT. That is what makes context.Canceled producible only by the handler's defer cancel() within test time.

doc_defects_found_by_executor.resolution: All five production interface methods and all seven test-fake methods migrated to context-first. The delegating fakes forward the caller's ctx rather than substituting context.Background(). Cost is small but it is real work the estimate does not price.

doc_defects_found_by_executor.severity: M2-affecting, NOT resolvable in M1 - flag for the M2 executor
doc_defects_found_by_executor.summary: AC4 demands 'r.Context()' >= 1 in BOTH handlers.go AND daemon.go, but design section 2.3's single-helper design puts 'r.Context()' in exactly ONE file.
doc_defects_found_by_executor.detail: Section 2.3 defines ONE readCtx helper and says all six store-reading GET handlers CALL IT - including handleHead, which lives in daemon.go. A call site spells 'd.readCtx(r)', not 'r.Context()'. AC7-style grep therefore reads >=1 in whichever file holds the helper body and 0 in the other. AC4's own parenthetical '(the helper; handleHead)' assumes handleHead spells r.Context() DIRECTLY, which contradicts the same section's 'all six ... call it'. Measured at end of M1 with readCtx in handlers.go: handlers.go 2 (the body at :219 plus a doc-comment mention at :213), daemon.go 0.
doc_defects_found_by_executor.resolution: NOT resolved in M1 - AC4 is M2's criterion and M1 must not green it. M1 placed readCtx in handlers.go so MU1 and MU2 keep their exact ONE-LINE mutation site, which is the property the plan calls load-bearing. M2 must either (a) satisfy AC4's daemon.go arm some other way, or (b) record AC4's grep form as unsatisfiable-as-written and rely on MU2's TestDaemonReadDisconnect, which is AC4's real mechanism. Moving r.Context() out to the six call sites would satisfy the grep but turn MU1/MU2 into six-line mutations.

doc_defects_found_by_executor.summary: V25 misplaces GetVerifyResult's only non-test caller: it is host/replay/replay.go:191, not :153. replay.go:153 is a GetObject call - and it is the ONE replay.go site the AC9 ratchet pins.
doc_defects_found_by_executor.detail: Measured: grep -rn '.GetVerifyResult(' host cmd -> replay.go:191 (production) plus 13 test sites. The claim's CONCLUSION (GetVerifyResult is off the daemon read path, so it stays context-free) survives; only the line number is wrong.
doc_defects_found_by_executor.resolution: No action. Recorded so a later reader does not conclude the ratchet's replay.go pin covers GetVerifyResult - it does not; GetVerifyResult is not one of the five getters the ratchet scans.

doc_defects_found_by_executor.summary: The busy_timeout injection makes a plain-path write DSN render as a file: URI, and it does not reach :memory: stores at all.
doc_defects_found_by_executor.detail: writeDSN previously returned the bare canonical path when len(params)==0 ('byte-identical driver behaviour to M1, modulo canonicalization', its own comment). Since the injection always adds one parameter, a production write handle is now always rendered as file:///abs/path?_pragma=busy_timeout%282000%29. Measured: the driver accepts it and PRAGMA busy_timeout reads back 2000 on both handles; the full suite is green. Separately, store.Open's in-memory carve-out calls openSQLite(path, path, ...) and never goes through writeDSN, so a :memory: store gets busy_timeout 0 - correct (a per-connection in-memory database has no cross-process lock contention) but it means T1.6 MUST be file-backed. journal_mode measured as 'delete', which is why BEGIN EXCLUSIVE actually excludes readers and T1.7's stimulus works at all.
doc_defects_found_by_executor.resolution: Kept, with the comment on writeDSN updated to state it. resolveDSN parses query parameters ONLY on the file: spelling, so a plain-path DSN with '?_pragma=...' silently discards it - T1.6's caller-override arm uses a file: DSN and carries a control asserting params are non-empty.

doc_defects_found.summary: The readStore seam is FIVE methods, not six. The design doc says 'six' twice and contradicts itself in the same paragraph.
doc_defects_found.detail: Section 2.5 layer 3 says 'a six-value read interface reads readStore'; section 2.7 says 'The single new Go surface is a six-method unexported interface'. MEASURED at d31362f: the six store-reading GET routes make SIX call sites but reach FIVE DISTINCT GETTERS - GetLogEntry serves both /v1/log/{index} (handlers.go:275) and /v1/log (handlers.go:323). The same section 2.5 paragraph says blockingStore overrides 'all five getters', and layer 4 says recordingStore overrides 'all five getters'. The 'six' is the ROUTE count leaking into a METHOD count - the iteration-86 class ('a count is only true inside the scope it was taken in') recurring inside the very document that records it.
doc_defects_found.resolution: Sprint plan section 0.5(i) fixes the seam at EXACTLY FIVE methods and names both wrong candidate sixths (Commit - the write path, DR-1 declares it untouched; GetVerifyResult - off the daemon read path, V25) plus the two out-of-seam ScanUnreadable* calls at daemon.go:392/414.
doc_defects_found.why_it_matters: NO acceptance criterion counts the interface's methods, so this defect cannot red a gate. An executor would either invent a sixth (widening the seam past ratified scope) or stall. It had to be settled in the plan or not at all.

doc_defects_found.summary: Three acceptance criteria (AC1, AC7, AC8) have NO named mutation anywhere in the doc's 12-row section 6 table, and AC4 has one only by implication.
